metaDescription: Six power stations for RV and camper use compared on capacity, 30A outlets, air conditioner startup surge, solar input, weight and how each one is charged.
expertTake: The BLUETTI Elite 300 is the best power station for an RV because it carries 3014Wh, a TT-30 RV outlet and a 12V 30A DC output in a compact case, while the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max is the value pick for weekend trailers. The Pecron F3000LFP is the capacity bargain for long stays. Owners who expect to run a rooftop air conditioner all night from a portable station should plan on far more capacity than any single unit here provides.
introParagraphs: An RV can use a power station in two very different ways: as a bolt-on supplement to a house battery bank, or as the main source of power for a small camper or van that has no real electrical system. The right size and connection depend entirely on which job it has.

Capacity alone is not enough. An RV owner needs the right outlets, enough surge to start a compressor, a sensible way to recharge on the road and a case that can be lifted into a bay. This guide compares six stations against those practical needs.

products.name: BLUETTI Elite 300 3014Wh 2400W RV Power Station

specList.label: Size
specList.value: Nearly 59 percent smaller than traditional large stations

products.description:
A TT-30 outlet, the 30 amp RV plug, is the feature that makes the Elite 300 genuinely RV-friendly, because it lets you run the trailer's shore cord straight from the station without an adapter dance. A high-current 12V 30A DC output also feeds the RV's 12V systems directly, avoiding inverter losses for lights, pumps and fans. It stores 3014 watt-hours in LFP cells and delivers 2400 watts with a 4800 watt surge.

That output is enough for a microwave, a coffee maker and a refrigerator at the same time, and a rooftop air conditioner with a soft start can run for a while, though not all night. The listing claims the case is nearly 59 percent smaller than traditional large stations, which matters when the storage bay is fixed. Against the 2048Wh EcoFlow Delta 3 Max it carries nearly half again the energy, and against the 3600Wh Delta Pro it is smaller and cheaper.

Plan the wiring: use a proper 30 amp cord, keep the station dry and ventilated, and set an alarm for the battery level. Recharge it from the tow vehicle, a generator or solar, and expect to lift it with two hands.
products.bestFor: Travel trailers and vans wanting 3kWh with a native 30 amp RV outlet.
pros: TT-30 RV outlet fits a trailer's shore cord
cons: Heavy for a two-hand lift into a bay
A rooftop air conditioner cannot run all night

products.name: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max 2048Wh 2400W Power Station
products.description:
Charging from empty to 80 percent in 1.13 hours means the Delta 3 Max can top up while you drive or while the generator runs for an hour, which is a practical match for RV life. It stores 2048 watt-hours in LFP cells, outputs 2400 watts and reaches 3400 watts in X-Boost mode for resistive loads. A sub-10 millisecond transfer keeps electronics steady when switching between shore power and battery.

For a weekend trailer it covers a refrigerator, lights, a fan and a microwave, but a rooftop air conditioner will drain it in a couple of hours. Compared with the 3014Wh Elite 300 it has less energy, no TT-30 outlet and a lower price, and against the 1191Wh UDPOWER it carries roughly double the energy. The ecosystem allows expansion later.

Bring an adapter for the RV plug if your trailer uses a 30 amp cord, and plan where it lives so ventilation is not blocked. Keep it indoors in cold weather, because charging below freezing is not supported. If the trailer has an existing converter, a short run from the tow vehicle's 12V line can keep the station topped up while you drive.
products.bestFor: Weekend trailers and vans wanting fast recharge and room to grow.
cons: 2048Wh cannot run an air conditioner for long

products.name: Pecron F3000LFP 3072Wh 3600W Power Station

specList.label: Outlets
specList.value: Six AC, two USB-C, two USB-A, car, two DC 5525

products.description:
Three kilowatt-hours and a 3600 watt pure sine inverter at a lower price than the big-name rivals is the Pecron's pitch, and the numbers back it up. It supports heavy appliances including refrigerators, microwaves and a soft-start air conditioner, and a full recharge takes about two hours from AC at 1800 watts, which the listing calls 30 percent faster than others.

Six AC outlets, two USB-C ports with 100 watt PD, two USB-A ports, a car port and two DC outputs let it serve an RV kitchen and a bedroom at once. Against the 3014Wh Elite 300 it has slightly more capacity and a stronger inverter, but lacks the dedicated TT-30 and 12V 30A outputs. Compared with the 2048Wh Delta 3 Max it offers more energy and output with less polish in the ecosystem.

Check the warranty terms and the app before buying, since the brand is less established. Keep the station level and ventilated, use a heavy cord for the air conditioner and treat the 3600 watt rating as a ceiling for short runs.
products.bestFor: Long RV stays where capacity and output matter more than ecosystem polish.
pros: Full AC recharge in about 2 hours at 1800W
Six AC outlets plus 100W USB-C PD
Powers up to 13 devices at once

products.name: EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3600Wh 3600W Power Station
products.description:
A 3600 watt-hour pack that can recharge in 1.8 hours from a 240 volt outlet or 2.7 hours from a standard wall outlet makes the Delta Pro the most capable station in the lineup for a big RV. Its 3600 watt AC output can expand to 4500 watts with companion hardware, and the unit can chain more battery capacity for long boondocking stays.

The cost is mass: it is a two-person lift and a fixture in a bay, not a sensible grab-and-go item. For a 30 amp rig it can run a microwave, a refrigerator and a soft-start air conditioner for a few hours, but an all-night cooling plan still needs more storage. Compared with the 3014Wh Elite 300 it holds more energy and output but has no TT-30 outlet, and next to the 3072Wh Pecron it offers a more mature ecosystem.

Consider a transfer switch and a proper 30 amp adapter, and keep the station inside the conditioned space where it will not overheat. Use solar or the generator to refill, and handle the weight carefully when loading.
products.bestFor: Large RVs and boondockers who want maximum capacity and expansion.
pros: Fast 1.8 hour charge on a 240V outlet
cons: Very heavy and awkward to move

products.name: Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 1024Wh Power Station

specList.label: Outlets
specList.value: Two pure sine AC, USB-C, USB-A, car

products.description:
Smaller trailers, truck campers and vans do not need three kilowatt-hours, and the Explorer 1000 v2 gives a sensible 1024 watt-hours in a case a person can carry with one arm. Its 1500 watt output and 3000 watt peak run a microwave, a coffee maker or a small induction burner, and a 50 minute fast charge makes it easy to refill from the vehicle or a generator.

A 10 millisecond UPS function keeps a router or a laptop running if shore power drops, which suits RV parks with unreliable pedestals. Against the 2048Wh Delta 3 Max it has half the energy, and against the 1191Wh UDPOWER it has slightly less energy but a stronger brand and support network. It will not run an air conditioner for any useful length of time.

Use it for lights, a fan, a fridge and electronics, and keep a separate plan for cooling. Store it where it stays above freezing in winter. Many owners pair it with a small folding panel and call it done for a long weekend of lights, a fan and a fridge.
products.bestFor: Vans, truck campers and small trailers with modest loads and light lifting.
pros: 1500W output with 3000W peak in a one-arm carry

products.name: UDPOWER S1200 1191Wh 1200W Power Station

specList.label: Outputs
specList.value: Five AC, four USB-A, two USB-C, two DC, one car

specList.label: Cycle claim
specList.value: At least 80 percent capacity retained over rated cycles

products.description:
Fourteen outputs mean the UDPOWER S1200 can replace the power strip in a camper, with five AC outlets, four USB-A ports, two USB-C ports, two DC outputs and a car outlet. The 1191 watt-hour LiFePO4 pack and 1200 watt pure sine output suit a small RV's electronics, a fridge and a few kitchen items.

A 400 watt solar input means a pair of roof or portable panels can top it up on a sunny day, and the battery is claimed to retain at least 80 percent of capacity across its rated cycles. Compared with the 1024Wh Jackery it has a bit more energy and many more outlets, and against the 3072Wh Pecron it is a third of the energy at a much lighter weight.

Read the manual for its AC input limits before relying on pass-through use, and check the brand's warranty terms. It suits a small camper that wants lots of ports and a modest battery. A short strap or a non-slip mat keeps it from sliding on rough roads, since the case has no tie-down points.
products.bestFor: Small campers wanting many ports and a modest, solar-friendly battery.
pros: Five AC outlets and 14 outputs total
1191Wh LiFePO4 pack with pure sine output
cons: 1200W cannot start a rooftop air conditioner
Less established brand with limited support

buyingCriteria.explanation: A rooftop air conditioner draws about 1300 to 1800 watts running and more at start, so a 3000Wh station lasts only about an hour and a half at that load. The BLUETTI Elite 300's 3014Wh and Pecron's 3072Wh stretch it a little, and anything near 1024Wh is not an option. Plan cooling around a generator or shore power.

A TT-30 outlet lets the trailer's own cord plug into the station, and a 12V 30A DC output feeds RV systems directly. Only the BLUETTI Elite 300 lists both, while others need adapters. Adapters work but add heat and failure points.

A station that takes 12 hours to refill is useless on a travel day. The Delta 3 Max charges to 80 percent in 1.13 hours, the Pecron fills in about 2 hours at 1800W and the Delta Pro in 1.8 hours at 3000W on 240V. Check which input you will have.

A 3kWh station is heavy, and lifting it into a bay is a real chore. The Jackery 1000 v2 and UDPOWER S1200 are one-person units, while the Delta Pro and Elite 300 are two-person lifts. Choose a spot before you buy. Strap it down with a rated cargo strap, because a sliding 40 pound battery is a hazard in a braking event.
Solar charging depends on input wattage and voltage window. The UDPOWER accepts up to 400W, the Delta 3 Max up to 500W. Match panel voltage and connectors to the unit.
A refrigerator or soft-start air conditioner needs surge. The Elite 300 lists 4800W surge, the Delta 3 Max 3400W in X-Boost and the Jackery 3000W peak. Match the surge to the biggest motor.

howWeEvaluated.title: RV integration
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked for TT-30 and 12V DC outputs that fit an RV. The BLUETTI Elite 300's TT-30 and 12V 30A put it ahead.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity and output
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared watt-hours and rated watts against RV appliance loads. The Delta Pro and Pecron lead, and the Jackery 1000 v2 suits smaller rigs.

howWeEvaluated.title: Recharge speed
howWeEvaluated.description: Road recharging decides whether a station is usable. The Delta 3 Max's 1.13 hours to 80 percent and the Pecron's 2 hour full charge led.

howWeEvaluated.title: Weight and fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered lifting and bay placement. Lighter units earned points for flexibility, and the Delta Pro lost some.

howToChoose.subheading: Single Station vs House Battery Bank

cards.label: Single station
cards.text: A Delta 3 Max or Elite 300 is portable, needs no wiring and can leave with you. It suits weekend use and rigs without a proper electrical system.

cards.label: House battery bank
cards.text: A permanent bank with an inverter gives more capacity and wiring integration for full-time living. It costs more and takes installation.

howToChoose.note: Choose a station for flexibility and a bank for full-time rigs.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Enough watt-hours for a night, a solar input that matches your panels and a refill path from the vehicle or generator. Skip air conditioning on battery.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Pecron and Elite 300 give three kilowatt-hours, the UDPOWER takes 400W of solar and the Delta 3 Max recharges fastest.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You stay off-grid for days or want a 30 amp plug. The Elite 300 and Delta Pro justify the premium.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You camp at hookup sites. The Explorer 1000 v2 handles the gaps.

maintenance.why: About 40 to 60 percent reduces cell stress. A full or empty pack ages faster.
A hot RV bay degrades cells, and charging below freezing can damage them.
A loose adapter heats under 30 amp loads. Replace worn cords.
Dust blocks cooling during fast charging.
App updates improve charge limits and fix bugs.

faq.q: Can a power station run an RV air conditioner?
faq.a: For a short time, yes, if the inverter can start the compressor. A 3000Wh station runs a 1500W air conditioner for roughly an hour and a half, so it is not an all-night solution.

faq.q: How big a station does a weekend trailer need?
faq.a: Add the daily watt-hours: a refrigerator about 800, lights and fans about 300 and electronics about 200. A 2000Wh station covers a weekend without air conditioning. Add a 25 percent margin for cold nights and cloudy days.

faq.q: Can I charge it while driving?
faq.a: Yes, through a 12V car socket or a DC-to-DC charger, but the current is limited, so it may add only a few hundred watt-hours per hour of driving.

faq.q: Do I need a TT-30 outlet?
faq.a: It is convenient, not required. An adapter works, but a native outlet avoids extra connections and heat. A short 30 amp adapter cord is cheap insurance.

faq.q: Is LiFePO4 better for an RV?
faq.a: Yes. It tolerates heat better and lasts thousands of cycles, which suits a battery that rides in a warm bay.

faq.q: Can I run it while charging?
faq.a: Many models support pass-through use, but it adds heat and wear. Use it for light loads, not as a routine way to run heavy appliances.
